subject: Resizing saved ggplots so its equivalent to a maximized view in R

messages.author: d3bb48bd374a955b
messages.subject: Resizing saved ggplots so its equivalent to a maximized view in R
parts:
I have a function that creates a ggplot graphic based on several
parameters and the saves the graphic to a png or pdf by calling the
pdf/png(), print(), and dev.off() functions. This is working great.

However, when I save the graphic, it prints it with a screen size
equal to the default unmaximized screen that shows up by just calling
a generic plot. My graphics are less overplotted/cluttered when I
maximize the plot viewing window inside of the standard R GUI.

How can I modify the pdf/png or print functions so that they will
print the maximized version of the graphic instead of the default
unmaximized version?

I know I can adjust the height, width, and resolution manually inside
of the pdf.png functions. However, I am having trouble finding the
optimal parameters. I feel it would be easier to just have some sort
of maximized screen setting size.

Thank you everyone in advance for your help! The relevant portion of
the code is included below:

emp_proficiency_plot <- ggplot(emp_subset, aes(x = date, y =
total_freq,
label = area, colour = date, size = total_freq)) +
geom_text(position = position_jitter(height=3, width = 0)) +
scale_size(to = c(2, 5)) +
opts(axis.text.x = theme_blank()) +
opts(axis.text.y = theme_blank()) +
xlab(paste("Employee:", parameter)) + ylab("Competency
Proficiency") +
opts(title = paste("Employee Competencies by Date:",
pub_date_start, "-", pub_date_end)) +
labs(colour = "Date") + labs(size = "Frequency")

pdf("C:/Users/bjvanov/Desktop/tester.pdf")
print(emp_proficiency_plot)
dev.off()}

parts:
Hi:

> args(ggsave)
function (filename = default_name(plot), plot = last_plot(),
device = default_device(filename), path = NULL, scale = 1,
width = par("din")[1], height = par("din")[2], dpi = 300,
keep = plot$options$keep, drop = plot$options$drop, ...)
NULL
> args(pdf)
function (file = ifelse(onefile, "Rplots.pdf", "Rplot%03d.pdf"),
width, height, onefile, family, title, fonts, version, paper,
encoding, bg, fg, pointsize, pagecentre, colormodel, useDingbats,
useKerning, fillOddEven, maxRasters)
NULL

Both of these graphics functions, as well as png(), jpeg(), et al.
have height and width arguments that are adjustable. Type
?ggsave
?pdf
?png
to access their individual help pages where the syntax is explained
and examples are shown.

HTH,
Dennis
